title: The Frohmanian Tether on SDiff(T^3): A Metriplectic Correction, Its Canonicity, and an Obstruction to Damping
notes: Copyright (c) 2026 Benjamin Stanley Frohman. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. This record is NOT a proof of global regularity of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations and makes no claim toward the Clay Millennium Problem.
description: PREPRINT (work in progress). Version 0.1.3 only adds this version's DOI (10.5281/zenodo.24102715) to the PDF's version note; Lean sources and certificate unchanged from 0.1.2 (10.5281/zenodo.24102345). ALL MAIN RESULTS ARE CONDITIONAL. Lean 4 (v4.30.0-rc1) / Mathlib (v4.30.0-rc1, rev 0c154d67103f74be3a0f2c509f72ccbf5be9f2a7) formalization of conditional statements about the Frohmanian tether T(F,G) = -kappa ||omega||^2 int <Pi_u dF, Pi_u dG>, a symmetric quadratic correction to the Arnold Lie-Poisson bracket. The functional derivative is the unique divergence-free L2 gradient along smooth compactly supported test fields (0 where none exists). Proved: symmetry and negative feedback (C3) unconditionally; nondegeneracy of T, polarization of T on functionals with gradients, saturation, projection-dependence and the canonical density of T; a family of smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free test fields curl(chi e_2) concentrated at any point with any radius, and with it the corrected weight condition AEEnstrophyWeight TetherKernel (every locally integrable density of T equals -kappa ||omega||^2 almost everywhere); the transported (equivariant) form of (C1), T(g.omega; F o g^-1, G o g^-1) = T(omega; F, G), for all translations (via translation equivariance of the functional gradient and of Biot-Savart); canonicity only inside a restricted kernel class (from diagonal saturation and polarization); and an obstruction to damping: every symmetric kernel satisfying (C2) has B(H,M) = 0 for every functional M. Refuted in Lean: (C1) with the functionals held fixed (for T, under translations), dH/dw = u, transitivity on Casimir levels, the pointwise strain bound |Du(x)| <= C ||omega||_inf, unrestricted polarization of T, the pointwise weight hypothesis, the a.e. weight hypothesis over all (possibly non-measurable) densities (Vitali-set density), and Step1Hyp; also removed: TetherIntegralPreserved, a circular Jacobi lemma, an antisymmetric uniqueness clause and a uniform lower bound on local existence times. Open hypotheses, by Lean name: (b) classical results not in Mathlib: KatoLocalWitness (hKato), BKMGlobalContinuation, SmoothPhysicalUniqueness, PeriodicBKMContinuation, KatoUniquenessOnExistenceTimes, IsCoadjointMotion; (d) as strong as the open problem: LocalTetherRate, LocalTetherBound, LocalTetherClosingBound, PeriodicTetherClosingBound, PeriodicDirectionDepletionBound, and the global-path forms FrohmanianTetherRate, FrohmanianTetherBound, FrohmanianTetherClosingBound, RiccatiMajorantExists; (c) kernel-class conditions on a competitor B in the canonicity theorems (PolarizesOnDifferentiable, SaturatesTetherQuadratic, h_proj, h_density, AEEnstrophyWeight B); open for T itself: DegenerateWRTKineticEnergy TetherKernel (C2) at regular vorticities, and transport-invariance under rotations and general volume-preserving diffeomorphisms (not formalized). No Jacobi identity is claimed.
